name: The Joe Rogan Experience

hosts.name: Joe Rogan
hosts.bio: Comedian, UFC color commentator and former Fear Factor host; has hosted JRE since 2009 out of his Austin, Texas studio.

audience_size: #1 podcast globally on Spotify for 2025 (sixth year running); PowerfulJRE YouTube ~21.15M subscribers (Sept 2026)
stances: Describes himself as socially liberal and anti-establishment; publicly endorsed Donald Trump in November 2024 and has hosted Trump, Kash Patel and other administration figures, while also criticizing some later policies. Frequently skeptical of mainstream media, pro free speech, pro hunting/fitness, open to psychedelics and UAP topics.

booking_contact.route: No public booking route. Rogan books through his personal network (comedians, fighters, scientists and prior guests). Producer Jamie Vernon ('Young Jamie') runs production and is widely cited as the person who sees guest suggestions; reach him only through a warm introduction. Do not cold-email.
booking_contact.notes: Reporting says joerogan.com used to have a guest-request contact form and it has been removed. A personal Gmail for Vernon circulates on third-party pages; we did not use it because it is not an official booking route. Best path: get Avery on the shows in this list that share JRE's guest pool (Theo Von, Flagrant, Shawn Ryan, Modern Wisdom, Tim Ferriss, Impaulsive) and get an intro from a host or a mutual past guest.

fit_angles.hook: How a street artist became a global brand: the Alec Monopoly playbook
fit_angles.why: Rogan likes outsider and underdog stories and how people built something from nothing, and the street-art-to-millions story is easy to follow.

fit_angles.hook: What's real and what's hype in the art market: pricing, flipping and celebrity collectors
fit_angles.why: Rogan often asks guests to take apart industries he sees as opaque or rigged, and a veteran dealer can explain how the market actually works.

fit_angles.hook: Selling blue-chip art online in 2014, before anyone trusted it
fit_angles.why: This is the show's usual tech-disruption theme told from an odd corner, and it leads naturally into NFTs and AI art.

avery_fit_notes: This is the end goal but realistically the last booking, because Rogan rarely takes cold pitches and almost never books business guests without a personal connection. Political topics are a live wire. Avery should stay with stories and the industry and avoid partisan positions.

hosts.bio: British entrepreneur who co-founded Social Chain and later founded Flight Story (media) and Flight Fund. He is a Dragons' Den investor and bestselling author.

audience_size: #2 podcast globally on Spotify for 2025; YouTube ~19.7M subscribers (Sept 2026)
topics: Rick Rubin on creativity and Jay-Z (Sept 21 2026)
AI debate: Ed Zitron, Andrew McAfee, Nate Soares, Roman Yampolskiy (Sept 17 2026)
David Bach on renting vs home ownership (Sept 2026)
Geopolitics: 'The Man Who Predicted The Iran War' (Sept 14 2026)
stances: Mostly apolitical, with a focus on business, health and psychology. Has drawn some criticism in the press for platforming health guests whose claims are disputed. Booking favors guests with a strong story and big credentials.

booking_contact.route: Email bookings@stevenbartlett.com (listed as the 'PR & Podcast Enquiries' address). The Podcast Bookings Manager is reported to be Jemima Erith.
booking_contact.notes: The bookings manager's name comes from a press report (https://www.diarydirectory.com/newsarticle/the-diary-of-a-ceo-podcast-names-podcast-bookings-manager/45074), so check it is still current. Lead with a story-driven hook and press credentials.

fit_angles.hook: Building a person into a brand: what I learned turning Alec Monopoly into a global business
fit_angles.why: Bartlett built his career on social-media brand building and loves founder origin stories that come with lessons.

fit_angles.hook: 'Click & Mortar': why the future of retail is social-first plus pop-ups
fit_angles.why: This is a clear marketing framework, the kind of tactical takeaway DOAC turns into clips.

fit_angles.hook: Art as an asset class: how the wealthy actually buy, hold and use art
fit_angles.why: DOAC's money episodes (David Bach and others) do well, and art investing is a fresh take on wealth.

avery_fit_notes: Strong thematic fit (marketing, brand building, founder story) and it has a real booking route. The bar is high, so the pitch needs a clear lesson and a framework rather than a bio. Low political risk.

name: This Past Weekend w/ Theo Von

hosts.name: Theo Von
hosts.bio: Comedian from Covington, Louisiana, first known from MTV's Road Rules/Real World Challenge. He now records in Nashville and is known for surreal storytelling and open-ended interviews.

audience_size: #2 podcast in the U.S. on Spotify for 2025; #5 globally
stances: Talks politics informally across the spectrum. He hosted Donald Trump in 2024 and NYC mayor Zohran Mamdani in 2026. Known for populist, working-class sympathies and curiosity about outsiders, hustlers and con stories.

booking_contact.route: Email tpwproducer@gmail.com (listed for podcast inquiries on the show's 'Be On the Show' page, which invites 'interesting or weird folks'). Mail: PO Box 40137, Nashville, TN 37204.
booking_contact.notes: The page also lists a fan hotline. Pitch with colorful stories rather than credentials.

fit_angles.hook: Wild stories from the art world: celebrity collectors, Monaco yachts and graffiti on Ferraris
fit_angles.why: Theo does best with colorful insider tales, and Alec Monopoly's rise is full of them.

fit_angles.hook: From hustler to dealer: how you sell a painting to a billionaire
fit_angles.why: Theo is fascinated by hustlers and con-adjacent trades (see the counterfeiter episode), and art dealing is a legitimate version of that world.

fit_angles.hook: Working with cops and kids: Miami Police 'Do the Right Thing' and Amigos for Kids
fit_angles.why: Theo often turns to working-class and youth struggles, so this gives the episode some heart.

avery_fit_notes: This is the best practical stepping stone to JRE because the pool of guests overlaps heavily and there is a public intake email. Avery needs to be a relaxed, funny storyteller. A buttoned-up business pitch won't land.
